chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud said:

I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Do I pray the two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf behind the Maqam (Station) where it is currently located, or where it was during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said, 'Where it is currently located.'

And whoever forgets these two rak'ahs or prays them elsewhere than the Maqam, then remembers them, he must return to the Maqam and pray them there, and it is not permissible for him to pray them elsewhere.
If he had already left Mecca and then remembered, if he is among those who are able to return to it, he should return and pray there.
And whoever is not able to do that, he should pray where he remembers, and there is no penalty upon him.

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The two rak'ahs of prayer following the obligatory circumambulation
key_terms.عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: During the time of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: Where should the two rak'ahs of Tawaf prayer be performed if one forgets or prays them in the wrong location?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific location for the two rak'ahs of Tawaf, affirming the current position of the Maqam Ibrahim as the designated spot for prayer. It provides a nuanced legal framework for negligence, distinguishing between those who can return to the Maqam to rectify their prayer and those who, having left Mecca, are exempted from penalty if they pray elsewhere. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on both precise ritual geography and practical ease (*rukhas*) in fulfilling obligatory acts.
